collection.description: An apprentice's examination under a strict mentor turns into a spectacular, harmless disaster.

r42.text: {K} {L} {M} (Subject) stands in the middle of the chaos and whispers, 'What could possibly go worse?' (Mentor) points at the ruined assignment. 'Do not ask that question again.'

r43.text: {K} The entire audience turns beet red. (Mentor) begins a magnificent scolding, only for a thunderclap to swallow every word. A sudden shower drenches the examination area. When it ends, (mentor) clears (mentor.his/her) throat. 'As I was saying...' (Subject) groans.

r44.text: {K} {L} The judges begin writing down a failure, but (subject) notices that the disaster has unexpectedly demonstrated the very principle the assignment was meant to test. After a long argument, the officials grant a pass. (Mentor) mutters, 'Do not ever do it that way again.'

r45.text: {K} {L} {M} (Subject) tries to explain that the result was at least memorable. 'Memorable is not the same as correct,' (mentor) replies. The examination ends in failure, and the village gains a story it will not soon forget.

r46.text: {K} {@Chief} turns red. The officials turn red. Even (mentor) turns red. (Subject) begins an apology, but an elder starts laughing so hard that the others join in. The verdict is still a failure, but nobody can pretend the afternoon was boring.

r47d.text: The cloth slips off at the worst possible moment. (Mentor) insists on an honest explanation, and (subject) finally gives one. The attempt fails, but the lesson sticks.

r47c.text: The officials leave without noticing the full extent of the damage. (Subject) cannot enjoy the apparent success and eventually admits what happened. The original work must be evaluated again.

r47.text: {K} (Subject) hastily throws a cloth over the evidence before the officials can inspect it.

r48.text: One mistake leads to another. Then another. By the time (subject) tries to stop the damage, the entire demonstration has become a sequence of increasingly ridiculous failures. {L} {M} (Mentor) finally says, 'We will begin again. On a different day.'

r49p.text: Working together, they save the essential part of the assignment. The judges allow the teamwork and grant a narrow pass.

r49f.text: They stop the situation from getting worse, but the assignment cannot be recovered. (Mentor) thanks the helper and tells (subject) to remember that asking for help is a skill too.

text_only.what: asking for help is a skill
text_only.reason: a figure of speech; the route's own small skill gain is made on the step after this page

r49.text: {K} (Subject) stands frozen until a nearby apprentice offers to help.

r50.text: {K} {L} (Subject) promises to fix everything immediately. The hurried repair creates an entirely new problem. {M} (Mentor) closes (mentor.his/her) eyes. 'You have somehow made a second examination out of the first.'

r51.text: {K} Before the officials can decide what to do, a tropical downpour forces everyone to shelter. (Subject) uses the delay to identify the mistake and explain a safer second attempt. (Mentor) agrees to schedule a new examination after the weather clears.

r52p.text: The examiner watches the corrected attempt and agrees to reconsider the verdict. (Subject) finally earns a pass.

r52f.text: The examiner sees the second attempt go wrong in a completely different way. 'I believe,' the examiner says gently, 'that you need more practice.'

r52.text: {K} The officials leave, faces burning with embarrassment. (Subject) stays behind and tries again, unaware that one examiner has returned for a forgotten bag.

r53.text: {K} {L} {M} The examination ends in failure. By sunset, the story has acquired three extra crashes, a flying pig, and a thunderstorm that lasted a week. (Subject) tries to correct the rumors, but nobody wants the less exciting version.

r54.text: {K} (Mentor) turns such a spectacular shade of red that (subject) forgets the disaster and asks if (mentor) is feeling well. The unexpected concern stops the scolding. After a moment, (mentor) sighs and helps (subject) understand the mistake.

r55.text: {K} {L} The oldest examiner unexpectedly bursts into laughter. 'I did something even worse when I was learning,' the examiner admits. The others demand the story. (Subject) still has to redo the assignment, but the room feels less frightening.

r56p.text: Instead of panicking, (subject) isolates the mistake, explains it, and completes the remaining work correctly. The officials reward the recovery rather than the original disaster.

r56f.text: (Subject) stops before the damage spreads. The assignment still fails, but (mentor) praises (subject.his/her) judgment in knowing when to stop.

r56.text: {K} (Subject) takes one breath and attempts a careful recovery while the officials watch.

r57.text: {K} {L} (Subject) whispers, 'At least nothing else can happen.' A thunderclap shakes the clearing. Everyone jumps. A parrot squawks. (Mentor) slowly points toward the sky. 'That,' (mentor) says, 'is why we do not tempt fate.'

"You failed. You scrutinized yourself too hard."
"I didn't get here overnight."
"Remember this always. Your own harshest critic is yourself."
"I will never admit this in public, but I was once like you."
"You were watching yourself so hard you forgot to watch the work."
"Nobody here was harder on you than you were."
"The first statue I ever carved fell over in front of {@chief}. I still carved the second."
"You're allowed to be bad at something before you're good at it."
"I shout because I care. You whisper to yourself because you care too much."
"Tomorrow, try being half as cruel to yourself as you were today."
"If you talk to yourself like that again, you'll answer to me."
"Mistakes are the price of learning. You've just paid a good amount."
"You can be disappointed without deciding you are hopeless."
"I asked you to make the work better, not to punish yourself."
"A mistake is something you made. It is not everything you are."
"If you knew how to do it perfectly already, you would not need a mentor."
"You have the right to ask a question before the work goes wrong."
"You noticed the error. That means you are learning to see."
"I would rather hear an honest failure than a beautiful excuse."
"Do not confuse being frightened with being unprepared."
"Your hands are shaking because this matters to you. Now give them a rest."
"The work is unfinished. That does not mean your future is."
"I can teach you to repair a mistake. I cannot teach you if you hide it."
"You are allowed to take pride in the parts you did well."
"The others are watching the lesson, not judging your whole life."
"I have ruined more projects than you have even attempted. That is how I learned."
"Tomorrow we will try again, and tomorrow I expect you to speak kindly to yourself."
"You listened to every criticism except the one that mattered: you needed rest."
"One day you will teach someone who is as frightened as you are now. Remember this."
"A careful worker knows when to begin again. A wise worker knows when to stop."
"You can respect the ancestors without pretending to know what they meant."
"An unanswered question is not a personal failure."
"Even the oldest scriptures have passages we still debate."
"You were so afraid of being wrong that you stopped listening."
"A respectful doubt is worth more than a confident guess."
"You do not have to settle three centuries of argument in one afternoon."
"The purpose of a ceremony is not to prove that you are perfect."
"A forgotten verse can be learned again. A frightened apprentice needs kindness."
"You are allowed to ask what a symbol means before you explain it."
"I have misread inscriptions older than your grandparents. The stones survived."
"Do not mistake the silence of the room for the judgment of the ancestors."
"You listened to everyone except yourself."
"You are here to learn the traditions, not carry every tradition alone."
"The wisest answer today might simply be that we do not know."
"Your work deserves care. You deserve patience."
